INCLUDE as impairment-specific assistive communication research, not merely generic text generation marketed to disabled users: section 5.2 explicitly designs noisy-input robustness for AAC mouth-stick/eye-tracker errors; section 6.1 tests dwell-constrained access based on eye-typing defaults; section 6.2 experimentally uses phrases written by people with ALS for voice banking. Section 4 additionally targets AAC language needs. Actual patient participants are absent and clinical benefit is not established, but the research design itself is adapted to impairment-specific communication.
